key_insight: GPT-4o’s gendered ADHD subtype associations differed between explicit and implicit cues, suggesting that cue framing can shape bias in self-diagnostic interactions.
clinical_relevance: Gender-sensitive responses could influence users’ understanding of ADHD, underscoring the need to evaluate demographic bias in medical AI tools.
method: Adapted the Context Association Test to ADHD self-diagnosis.
Evaluated GPT-4o in a zero-shot setting.
Compared ADHD associations under explicit and implicit gender cues.
evidence_signal: Explicit cues consistently amplified certain ADHD subtype associations, while implicit cues produced distributions close to the study’s proxy reference.
watch_item: Bias-mitigation overcorrection is a proposed explanation, not a demonstrated mechanism; the abstract does not establish diagnostic accuracy or patient outcomes.
paper_title: Gender Associations in LLM-Mediated ADHD Self-Diagnosis
